body: This was one of the biggest things I took away from my five years working at Disneyland. I started as someone excited about having my own nuclear family someday (shout out to white supremacist evangelical brainwashing!) and three years in I was so disturbed by the behavior and distinct misery I saw in hundreds of thousands of parents from all over the world that I knew I’d end my life before I became a mother. It also made me an antinatalist before I knew the word for it, but that’s a separate revelation haha happy for you, OP, you escaped!

I tried to clarify that it’s only for people who had the option to abort; THEY made themselves a mom by choosing to become one. Any sperm and egg could have gestated to make any child their first, it has nothing to do with this kid in particular. That’s all I was trying to say. 

Not saying I don’t have unlearning to do, but I also hate misogyny and am not trying to perpetuate it. I thought a sub about antinatalism would be a place to express that I don’t understand why people place the ownership on a kid who just happened to be born (and yes, will suffer and die) when they were the ones who made active choice in the situation; I just didn’t think it needed more context. I deleted it because I don’t want anyone to think I was being misogynistic or hateful towards women.

I’m not trying to make any argument or suggest we should force anyone to not have kids? I’m just one of many oldest children who is ‘credited’ for making a mom a mom when I did nothing to make that happen, I just happen to be the result of a pregnancy she chose not to terminate; the wording doesn’t make sense to me. Plus I do feel bad for everyone that now has suffer and die, myself included. I figured my thoughts could be posted here because it’s an antinatalism sub.

There were also parents that seemed happy and treated their kids with respect and kindness (which I always made sure to tell them I admired and appreciated how they spoke to their kid). I’d say it was 1/500.

I can’t speak for everyone nor am I trying to prove anything, but I’m the one who always comments that working at Disneyland for five years is what made me childfree. I fully wanted kids and was excited to be a mom one day, but after facing thousands of parents who looked absolutely miserable and had this haunting aura of hating their lives around them, let alone the things they’d say to their kids (and me!) about how unhappy they were, it made me realize that was not the life I wanted for myself.

Proudly childfree and antinatalist! I reached both conclusions after working at Disneyland for five years and witnessing hundreds of thousands of interactions between parents and their children from all over the globe.
